final.title: Why subscription sprawl survives in small teams
final.body:
Subscription sprawl usually survives because it sits in the background of back-office work. Someone signs up for a tool, the renewal date gets noted badly or not at all, and the review keeps slipping behind invoices, admin, and everything that looks more urgent. In a small business, that is usually a visibility problem before it is a software problem.

For an owner-operator, the bounded decision is simple: can you list every active subscription and its renewal date right now? If not, the first step is a one-time manual audit. Make the list in a spreadsheet, include the owner and renewal date, and get it clean before you think about automation. If yes, the next question is whether you need a simple reminder flow, a searchable register, or a quarterly review that keeps the list honest.

That is the kind of workflow Bareni looks at: one recurring process, one clear owner, and a control that stays inside human approval. If the list is already small and tidy, a spreadsheet may be enough. If it is messy, start with the audit first. Tiny bit of unglamorous work, but it keeps you from automating confusion.
